samples.summary: `Fix rounds used: N of 0` — the maxRounds guard is defeated because Number(null) === 0 is finite
samples.evidence: renderLoopStatus gates the budget line on `Number.isFinite(Number(failedRounds)) && Number.isFinite(Number(maxRounds))` (line 196). `maxRounds` defaults to `null` and main() explicitly passes `null` when `--max-rounds` is absent or empty (lines 335-337), but `Number(null) === 0`, which IS finite — so the line renders as `**Fix rounds used:** 2 of 0`. Both new call sites in .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml omit `--max-rounds` entirely (`--event ci-paged`, line 192; `--event ci-fix-pushed`, line 396), so every CI-arm update writes a nonsensical `of 0` budget onto the sticky dashboard. The sibling file guard-verdict.mjs deliberately implements `n()` to avoid exactly this Number(null)===0 trap, so the intent was clearly `null means not measured`; renderLoopStatus omits that treatment. Fix: test with `v !== null && v !== undefined && v !== "" && Number.isFinite(Number(v))` (or reuse the same `n()` helper).

samples.summary: `ready` conflates "not a draft" with "promoted", so a non-draft managed PR always reads "ready for human review" even when the panel just requested changes
samples.evidence: main() computes `ready: prView.isDraft === false` (line 339) and renderLoopStatus gives `ready` precedence over the caller's event (lines 189-193) and over the newest round's "Then" cell, which becomes `🤝 promoted` (line 221). The panel does not only run on draft agent branches: agent-review-panel.yml's gate admits any PR carrying `agent:managed` ("@claude loop", lines 179-186), and those human PRs are normally NOT drafts. For such a PR the dashboard headline reads "ready for human review" and the current round reads "🤝 promoted" while `--event panel` carried "Panel requested changes" — i.e. the surface built to replace log-reading states the opposite of the verdict. The same wrong state occurs on an already-promoted agent PR that receives a new commit and a blocking round. `prView.state` is fetched but never used, so a closed/merged PR reads as ready too. Ready should be derived from the promotion signal (non-draft AND panel not blocking / the `promoted` event), not from `isDraft` alone.

samples.summary: The paged projection only recognises the REVIEW latch, so a CI-arm page (`<!-- agent-paged -->`) never self-heals into the sticky comment
samples.evidence: `const paged = comments.some(isPagedLatchComment)` (line 318) uses rounds.mjs's `isPagedLatchComment`, which matches only `PAGED_LATCH = "<!-- agent-review-paged -->"` (rounds.mjs:41,73). The CI arm pages with a DIFFERENT marker, `<!-- agent-paged -->` (.github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml:133,146 and :369). So after the CI-fix loop pages a human, the only reason the comment shows "🛑 paged" is the transient `--event ci-paged` string passed by that one step; any later update — the review panel still runs on such a PR, because agent-review-panel.yml's gate latch also checks only `agent-review-paged` (line 220) — re-derives `paged = false` and rewrites the headline to "review panel finished" / "ready for human review". That directly breaks the file's stated invariant that the comment is re-derived in full from the unforgeable paged latch and that "a missed update self-heals on the next one": for the CI arm it un-heals instead. Both markers need to be checked here.

samples.summary: Unprotected `core.summary...write()` was added inside the CI attempts-guard decision step, so a summary-write failure can kill the decision (and leave a paged PR unlabelled)
samples.evidence: The three new `await core.summary.addRaw(...).write()` calls (lines 138, 150, 155) run inside the `Attempts guard` github-script step, which is NOT continue-on-error. `write()` throws if it cannot write (`@actions/core` throws when GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY is unset or the append fails). In the PAGED branch the write is placed AFTER `issues.createComment` but BEFORE `core.setOutput('paged','true')` (lines 144-152): a throw there leaves the page comment posted while `paged` is never set, so "Set state → blocked (paged)" and the paged effort summary both skip — a paged PR with no `agent:blocked` label. In the PROCEED branch a throw prevents `proceed=true` (line 156), so the whole CI-fix round is skipped and, because every downstream page step is gated on `proceed == 'true'`, nothing pages (this loop has no stalled net). Contrast review-round-guard.mjs, where the same display concern is routed through `appendStepSummary`, which is explicitly try/catch'd "so a full disk or bad path must not fail the guard" (guard-verdict.mjs:118-126). The github-script writes deserve the same try/catch.

samples.summary: On a hard fixer error the fix-outcome status note points at a page comment that has not been posted
samples.evidence: "Page if the fix produced no commit" (line 1695) deliberately has NO `always()` — the comment says a hard fixer error must fall through to the `stalled` net instead of double-paging. The new "Update loop status (fix outcome)" step (line 1727) DOES use `always()`, so when the fixer step fails and the branch head did not move it writes `EVENT=paged` with "paged to a human (see the page comment)" (line 1743) at a moment when no page comment exists on the PR; the actual page only arrives later from the `stalled` job. A reader following the note finds nothing. Either mirror the page step's condition (`success() && ...`) or word the note as "the pipeline will page".

samples.summary: Dead branch: the "→ (omitted row)" fallback in the round table can never be reached
samples.evidence: Line 216 computes `next = isNewest ? null : (i + 1 < shown.length ? shown[i + 1] : null)`. `isNewest` is true exactly when `roundNo === rounds.length`, i.e. only for `i === shown.length - 1`; for every other `i`, `i + 1 < shown.length` is necessarily true, so `next` is never null on the non-newest path and the `"→ (omitted row)"` fallback at line 229 is unreachable. Harmless, but it encodes a case the author believed existed and hides that the oldest SHOWN row correctly links forward while truly-omitted rows are handled by the note at line 234.

samples.summary: The displayed fix-round budget is computed over ALL manifest lenses, while the enforced budget counts only the round's required checks — the two can disagree
samples.evidence: `countFailedReviewRounds(commits, lensCheckNames, ...)` (line 321) is passed `lensCheckNamesFrom()` — every lens in lenses.json (line 265). The guard that actually enforces the cap passes `requiredCheckNames`, the per-round APPLICABLE subset (review-round-guard.mjs:35,226, fed by `needs.review-panel.outputs.required_checks`). A historical commit whose failing lens is no longer applicable to the current diff is therefore counted by the dashboard but not by the guard, so the comment can read "Fix rounds used: 3 of 3" while the guard proceeds (or vice-versa). Since the whole point of the surface is to explain the loop's budget, the two counts should be derived from the same name set (pass the required checks through, as the panel/promote steps already have them).

samples.summary: Upsert has no concurrency protection, so two overlapping updates can post two sticky comments (and one silently overwrites the other's projection)
samples.evidence: `comments` is fetched at line 309 and the existence check happens at line 357; the read-then-write window spans an unbounded number of check-run API calls (line 316 loops over every commit). Two loop-status invocations that overlap (e.g. the CI arm's `ci-fix-pushed` update for one CI run and the review-panel arm's `panel` update for another, which are different workflows and not covered by any shared concurrency group) will both find no existing comment and both POST, leaving two sticky dashboards — after which `comments.find(isOwnStatusComment)` always updates the first one and the second goes stale forever. A duplicate is also unavoidable if a PATCH races a POST. Cheap mitigation: re-list immediately before the write, or key on the newest matching comment.

samples.summary: Every status update spends one check-runs request per PR commit, so on a long-lived PR the dashboard silently bails out on rate limits
samples.evidence: Line 316 (`for (const c of commits) c.checkRuns = checkRunsFor(c.sha)`) issues at least one paginated API call per commit on every invocation, and this change adds up to five invocations per round (panel, round-guard, fix outcome, promote, stalled). A 60-commit PR therefore costs ~300 extra REST calls per round. Any 403/secondary-rate-limit throws inside the try block and is swallowed by `bail()` (line 348), which exits 0 — the dashboard just stops updating, and because the caller is `continue-on-error` nothing anywhere reports it. Bounding the walk to the newest MAX_ROUND_ROWS commits (the table only renders 15) would remove most of that cost.

verdict.reason: The finding is accurate in every checkable particular. loop-status.mjs:196 gates the budget line on `Number.isFinite(Number(failedRounds)) && Number.isFinite(Number(maxRounds))`; since `Number(null) === 0` is finite, the `null` default (line 179) and the explicit `null` produced by main() at lines 335-337 (missing flag → `Number(undefined)` = NaN → null; empty flag → `!== ""` false → null) both pass the guard, so line 198 emits `**Fix rounds used:** N of 0`. Both agent-iterate-ci.yml call sites are real and omit --max-rounds: line 192 (`--event ci-paged`, only --note/--run-url) and line 396 (`--event "$EVENT"` for ci-fix-pushed/paged, only --note/--run-url). No caller-side or downstream guard prevents the bad render, and loop-status.test.mjs only covers maxRounds: 3 (lines 123, 128), so nothing catches it. This is an in-lane wrong-condition bug producing clearly wrong output on a live path; impact is display-only on a projection comment (never read back as a gate, per the file's docblock lines 7-11), so it sits at the lower end of major, but I have no named ground to refute it.
